a scan without this family's findings is NOT evidence of cleanliness FArgType => 1 finding across the eight trees (0534); no false-positive audit recorded FOpMismatch => 9 findings across the eight trees (0534); a scan without this family's findings is NOT evidence of cleanliness FCondBool => has never produced a finding on the pinned corpora or on this tree (measured, 0534); a scan without this family's findings is NOT evidence of cleanliness FUnreachable => ZERO module-view findings across the eight trees (0534, re-measured 0555) and ZERO per-function findings after 0557, which FIXED the over-report 0555 pinned: a `match`'s arms are not evaluated (0469, 0502), so a value assigned only inside an arm read as DEFINITELY unassigned and a later `if` on it committed to one side -- the over-report was on `src/parser/parser.mbt:4221`, and 0557 collects what an arm's body MAY WRITE (the names, syntactically, WITHOUT evaluating the arm) and widens the names that are already bound, so the finding is gone and the regression row (pipeline_0555_test) now asserts the ABSENCE of it; a scan without this family's findings is still NOT evidence of cleanliness FStaleNosec => has never produced a finding on the pinned corpora or on this tree (measured, 0534); a scan without this family's findings is NOT evidence of cleanliness FInfeasibleBranch => has never produced a finding on the pinned corpora or on this tree (measured, 0534); it fires on hand-written contradiction fixtures, so this is a statement about REACH on real code and not about the emitter FRedundantGuard => has never produced a finding on the pinned corpora or on this tree (measured, 0534); it fires on hand-written implication fixtures, so this is a statement about REACH on real code and not about the emitter FDeadStore => 29 findings across the corpora before its first audit, of which 20 were ONE defect in the CFG rather than in this family (0531), leaving 9; those nine were then measured one by one (0532) and all nine are gone: eight were a read inside a region the frontend declared outside its subset, and the ninth was the index of a place-store not counted as a read (0542). The family then reported ZERO across the pinned corpora. 0565 taught it about DECLARATIONS -- a `let` whose value is overwritten before any read -- and it now reports 23 findings across the pinned corpora, all of them on moonbitlang/core, and every one of them was measured against its source and is a true positive. A scan without its findings is not evidence that no write is dead FDivisionByZero => NEW in 0571, and built from the lecture's own example (`Introduction`, Nanjing University, p.45-58): the divisor of a division or a remainder is DEFINITELY zero -- zero on every path that reaches the operation. The seven pinned corpora hold 3,138 division and remainder operators and 21,658 subscripts (a syntactic count, 0571), and every LITERAL zero divisor among them is one float modulo (`moonbitlang/core` `builtin/double_mod_test.mbt:44`), three block comments or one string -- so the shape this family looks for is not in the corpus. MEASURED on the eight pinned trees (0571): the family fires on ZERO findings, and the reason is measured rather than guessed. The seven pinned corpora hold 3,138 division and remainder operators and 21,658 subscripts (a syntactic count, 0571), and the only REAL negative subscripts among them are three -- `moonbitlang/core` `deque/panic_test.mbt:27`, `deque/panic_test.mbt:32` and `immut/vector/panic_test.mbt:39` -- and all three are inside `test` blocks, which this frontend declares outside its subset and does not analyse. MEASURED on the eight pinned trees (0587): the family fires on ZERO findings, and the reason is measured rather than guessed: the corpora are scanned with NO taint specification, because a source and a sink are FUNCTIONS OF THE ANALYSED PROJECT and no corpus declares which of its functions they are. name: match
detail: match self { FParse => the text could not be read as the analysed subset, or was deliberately not read FUndefinedName => a name used here resolves to no visible binding FUnusedLocal => a local is assigned but never read in its function FUnusedParam => a parameter is never read in its function FParamChanged => a parameter is assigned inside its own function FAssignType => the assigned value's type is not assignable to the target FArgType => an argument's type is not assignable to the callee's parameter FOpMismatch => the operand or result types are outside what the operator is defined for FMethodError => no method matching the operands exists on their concrete types FCondBool => a condition's type is not Bool FUnreachable => UNREACHABLE CODE, in the deck's sense: a statement that no execution reaches, because the flow arriving at it has already left the block FStaleNosec => a nosec comment suppressed nothing FInfeasibleBranch => no input reaches this branch: the guards on the way to it contradict it, so its domain D[P] is empty FRedundantGuard => the guards before this test already force its outcome, so the test cannot decide anything FDeadStore => the value this write put in the name is read on no path before the name is written again or the function exits -- and a DECLARATION is one write: the value the initialiser bound is dead in exactly the same way FDivisionByZero => the divisor of this division is zero on EVERY path that reaches it, so the division fails at run time FNegativeIndex => the index of this subscript is negative on EVERY path that reaches it, so the subscript is out of bounds at run time FTaintFlow => tainted data may reach a sensitive argument of a sink: the source's result is tainted data, and the sink's argument may hold it}

name: match
detail: match self { FParse => the declared subset is exactly what the frontend can read, and everything outside it is reported rather than assumed analysed FUndefinedName => the visible binding set is complete: this file, the extern .mbti tables, the builtins -- confidence is low because the conclusion rests on names, not declarations FUnusedLocal => the frame audit saw every read, and no unread region could reach the declaration FUnusedParam => the function contains no unread region, so no read could have been missed FParamChanged => the assignment was observed directly, which an unread region cannot undo FAssignType => both types are known; an unknown type on either side absorbs the error FArgType => the callee's signature is known: declared in this file, or in the extern .mbti tables FOpMismatch => neither operand is unknown, and both types are within the operator table FMethodError => both operands are concrete; an unknown operand absorbs FCondBool => the condition's type is known, and the branch was not constant-folded FUnreachable => the behavioral lens executes the body and joins branches, so a terminator inside a BRANCH does not by itself kill what follows -- the join is over ONE execution, EXCEPT that a condition naming a parameter bound from the caller's argument is no longer allowed to commit the frame (0537): both sides are explored and their flows joined, so such a condition cannot kill what follows on its own FStaleNosec => a suppression matches a report on the same start line whose family it names FInfeasibleBranch => facts come only from a guard comparing an IMMUTABLE local binding against a LITERAL, within one function; a rebound, aliased or non-literal operand carries no fact FRedundantGuard => the same fragment: an immutable binding against a literal, with integer comparisons that do not wrap and no reassignment between the two guards FDeadStore => a BACKWARD MAY analysis over this function body's control-flow graph: not-live is the trustworthy direction, so a read the graph does not model can only make this report wrong, and every such case is named in excluded. A DECLARATION is reported only when the name is read SOMEWHERE -- that second half is what keeps this family off the lines `UnusedLocal` owns, whose claim is 'never read anywhere' FDivisionByZero => the divisor's sign is DETERMINED by the sign domain's transfer functions, and the domain's top -- unknown -- is never reported, so a finding means the divisor's sign was pinned to zero and not merely guessed. The analysis is INTRAPROCEDURAL over one function body's control-flow graph, so a divisor that becomes zero only after a CALL is not seen; and the two function-level guards apply as they do to the dead-store family: a statement the graph did not convert, and a region the frontend did not read, each make the whole function unanalysed FNegativeIndex => the index's sign is DETERMINED by the sign domain's transfer functions, and the domain's top -- unknown -- is never reported, so a finding means the index's sign was pinned to negative and not merely guessed. The analysis is INTRAPROCEDURAL over one function body's control-flow graph, so an index that becomes negative only after a CALL is not seen; and the two function-level guards apply as they do to the dead-store family: a statement the graph did not convert, and a region the frontend did not read, each make the whole function unanalysed FTaintFlow => the tainted datum was created by a call to a SOURCE, and the sink's argument MAY hold it -- a MAY claim, so a finding means the flow could NOT be ruled out, not that it certainly happens. The tainted datum is an OBJECT (the deck's own p.71-72) and it is propagated by the tree's pointer analysis, so the propagation is flow-insensitive and context-insensitive. The analysis is INTRAPROCEDURAL over one function body's control-flow graph, so a source in one function and a sink in another are not connected, and the three function-level guards apply as they do to the dead-store family: a statement the graph did not convert, a region the frontend did not read, and a file the frontend did not read whole, each make the whole function unanalysed}

name: match
detail: match self { FParse => nothing about the skipped construct's meaning: a notice is not a defect, and one notice per construct does not enumerate what is inside it FUndefinedName => names a dependency or a macro could bind; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for an undefined state name FUnusedLocal => reads inside a region the parser cut in half; a write-only binding is still reported FUnusedParam => any read in a function whose text contains an unread region -- the whole function is silenced FParamChanged => the same as UnusedParam: an unread region silences it, even though an observed assignment cannot be un-observed FAssignType => unannotated rebinding, which widens with a join; and field assignment targets, which are unchecked FArgType => calls to a callee with no visible signature -- those are counted unchecked, not reported; and named-call arity FOpMismatch => unknown operand types; the pipe operator and regex-match operands are exempt FMethodError => a call outside the per-file method table; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for a call on a state operation FCondBool => constant-folded conditions and unknown types; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for a non-boolean guard FUnreachable => DEAD CODE in the deck's sense -- executed but irrelevant, a value overwritten before use -- is reported by NO family, this one included; path feasibility, which needs semantics and is undecidable in general, is reported under MSA-013 only when a BOUNDED constraint model can show the domain empty; and THIS FAMILY OVER-REPORTED when a callee's parameter was bound from the caller's argument until 0537, which made a condition naming a caller-bound parameter explore both sides and join instead of committing -- that defect is FIXED and its regression row now asserts the absence of the finding (pipeline_0524_test); 0555 FIXED the second over-report, the `if`'s PATH JOIN -- the fall-through path was missing from the join and an alternative branch started from the then-branch's environment, so a value assigned only inside a branch read as DEFINITELY assigned after the `if` -- and its regression rows assert the absence of that finding (pipeline_0555_test); 0557 FIXED the third over-report, the one 0555 pinned: a `match`'s arms are not evaluated, so a value assigned only inside an arm read as DEFINITELY unassigned and a later `if` on it committed to one side -- what an arm MAY WRITE is now collected syntactically, WITHOUT evaluating the arm, and the names already bound are widened, so the finding is gone (pipeline_0555_test, row 'a match arm that is never evaluated no longer over-reports'); a condition built from a source literal still folds, so an `if` whose every branch terminates still kills what follows; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for a state outside the reachability closure FStaleNosec => whether the suppressed finding was real FInfeasibleBranch => feasibility that needs a call result, an index, an arithmetic identity or an interprocedural fact -- undecidable in general, so a branch this model cannot decide is counted UNDECIDED rather than claimed reachable FRedundantGuard => the same fragment; a test whose operand was mutated after the binding carries no fact, so it is undecided rather than reported FDeadStore => reads this graph does not model: a break or continue edge is a Stop, a nested function body is its own graph, and a read through a field or index alias is not tracked -- so the store is a candidate rather than a proof of uselessness, and a right-hand side with effects is unaffected by the finding. A FUNCTION THAT HOLDS A REGION THE FRONTEND DID NOT READ IS NOT ANALYSED AT ALL: an if used as a value, an anonymous function literal and a try expression each leave a hole in the function that contains them, and a read inside such a hole is a path this graph never saw (0542). A DECLARATION WHOSE NAME IS NEVER READ ANYWHERE IS `UnusedLocal`'s FINDING, not this one, and the 'read somewhere' that decides it is the GRAPH's -- so a read the graph does not model makes a declaration look unread as well as a store (0565) FDivisionByZero => a divisor whose sign the analysis could NOT pin down is not reported, and that is most of the cases: a parameter, a value read from a field, a value returned by a call, and a value that is zero on one path and not on another -- the last one because the sign domain JOINS the two paths and the join of zero and anything else is unknown. A FLOAT DIVISION BY ZERO IS NOT A CRASH, and the family does not report one the source shows to be a float: `1.0 / 0` is Infinity and `1.0 % 0` is NaN (MEASURED against the toolchain, 0571), while `1 / 0` raises `divide by zero` and `1 % 0` raises `remainder by zero`. THE RESIDUAL IS THE TYPE LENS'S: it publishes the types of the MODULE's names and not of a function's locals, so a float-valued LOCAL divided by a definitely-zero value is reported even though it does not crash -- and the eight pinned trees contain no such division (measured, 0571). A DIVISION INSIDE A REGION THE GRAPH DOES NOT MODEL is not analysed at all: a block used as a value holds statements the graph never turned into nodes, so a name such a block assigns would still carry its old value in the state this analysis reads FNegativeIndex => an index whose sign the analysis could NOT pin down is not reported, and that is most of the cases: a parameter, a value read from a field, a value returned by a call, and an index that is negative on one path and not on another -- the last one because the sign domain JOINS the two paths and the join of negative and anything else is unknown. A SUBSCRIPT INSIDE A REGION THE GRAPH DOES NOT MODEL is not analysed at all, for the reason the division's is: a block used as a value holds statements the graph never turned into nodes. A subscript of a NEGATIVE index is out of bounds in every container this language has, and the toolchain does not catch it: `moon check` exits 0 on `arr[-1]` FTaintFlow => IMPLICIT FLOWS (the deck's p.47-58): a branch on tainted data, a termination channel, a timing channel and an exception channel are NOT analysed, and that boundary is the DECK'S OWN (p.61-62: 'Explicit flows generally carry more information than covert channels, so we focus on explicit flows'). The analysis does not model what a CALL RETURNS, so the tainted datum reaches a VARIABLE only when the source call IS the right-hand side of the assignment; a source call that IS the sink's argument is read directly. A DERIVED VALUE IS NOT MODELLED EITHER: the deck's OWN chapter-2 example (p.40: `cmd = "..." + x; execute(cmd)`) is NOT reported -- in the concatenation form AND in the interpolation form -- while the same program with the derived value REMOVED IS, and the three are MEASURED and pinned by `src/pipeline/taintdeck_test.mbt`. A concatenation allocates a NEW string and an interpolated string carries a REFERENCE, so the tainted datum never enters the derived variable's points-to set; and the deck's own rule table (p.75) has four rules and none of them is a rule for a derived value. A FUNCTION WHOSE GRAPH LOST A STATEMENT IS NOT ANALYSED AT ALL, because the statement it lost may have been a SANITIZER -- a `pw = scrub(pw)` the analysis never read would leave the tainted datum in `pw`, and the flow reported would be one the program does not have. THE SECURITY LEVELS (the deck's p.25-28) and the NONINTERFERENCE property (p.29-36) are not analysed either: a level is a LATTICE element and a policy is an ORDER on it, this analysis's label is a single bit, and noninterference is a RELATIONAL property over TWO RUNS of the program}

name: match
detail: match self { FParse => Advice::{ why : The frontend did not read a construct, or a file-kind frontend rejected a shape. On a .mbt this marks the FIRST genuine read failure in the file: every finding at or after that line is withheld, because it would be derived from an already-wrong tree. On .mbti / .mbt.md / .mbtp it is a frontend rule (malformed line, duplicate signature, unresolvable type reference) rather than a parse boundary., how : Fix the FIRST parse error only — it is the boundary, and later ones are frequently its consequences. If the message is 'test declaration is outside the analyzed subset' or 'struct declaration is outside the analyzed subset', it is a declared scope limit of this analyzer, not a defect: there is nothing to fix, and the finding is rendered 'notice:' rather than 'error:' for exactly that reason. If it is 'unknown type ... in interface signature', the .mbti lens has no cross-file awareness and the type may well be declared in a sibling package; treat that finding as unverified rather than acting on it.,} FUnusedLocal => Advice::{ why : A local binding was assigned and never read anywhere in the function. The scan is not flow-sensitive, so a read inside an unreachable or dead branch still counts as a use., how : Remove the binding, or read it. A name that starts with `_` is exempt, matching the compiler: a discard binding (`let _ = f(x)`, a `for k, _ in pairs` binder, or the unused second half of `let (count, _classes) = refine()`) is how MoonBit says 'I mean to drop this', so reporting it would contradict the toolchain. Verified by probe, not assumed — `moon check` stays silent on `_f` / `_classes` while warning on a `plain` control in the same file. This wording reversed the rule in 0.4.13; before that, an underscore-PREFIXED name was reported on the reasoning that 'a name is not a discard pile', which the toolchain does not agree with.,} FUnusedParam => Advice::{ why : A parameter was never read in the function body. Writing THROUGH a parameter counts as a read, so `self.field = v` and `v[0] = x` do not trigger this; only a parameter that is genuinely never touched does., how : Remove the parameter and its argument at every call site, or keep it for signature compatibility and accept the warning. A parameter named exactly `_` is exempt — the same discard idiom as locals; an underscore-PREFIXED name is not exempt. This wording reversed the rule in 0.4.13: a probe settled that `moon check` does NOT warn on an unused `_f`, only on a non-underscore control in the same file, so the prefix is exempt here too.,} FParamChanged => Advice::{ why : A parameter's BINDING was rebound by a bare assignment — `p = expr` or `p += 1` — so from the next read on, `p` names something the caller never passed. Writing THROUGH a parameter is not this: MoonBit structs are references, so `self.field = v`, `v[0] = x` and `pair.0 = x` mutate the object the parameter points at and leave the parameter itself alone, and those do not report., how : If the rebinding is deliberate, accept the finding as advisory. If you meant to reach a field or an element, write that target directly instead of the parameter. If you need the original value after the write, copy it first: `let mut copy = p`, then assign to `copy` — that is also the fix for a genuine rebind, because it makes the change local to the call.,} FAssignType => Advice::{ why : The right-hand side's inferred type is not assignable to the declared annotation. `Unknown` is always assignable, so a finding here means both sides were resolvable and disagreed., how : Correct the annotation, or convert the value. Caveat: optional types (`String?`) and the `None` literal are not modelled by the type lens, so a `None` passed into an optional parameter can be typed as something unrelated and report here; verify against `moon check` before acting.,} FArgType => Advice::{ why : Either an argument's type is not assignable to the declared parameter, or more arguments were passed than the signature declares. The 'too many arguments' form only runs against a REAL parameter list — a function known only through a `.mbti` declaration is typed as an unknown-signature value and is never arity-checked., how : Check the declared parameter type at the call site. If this is an 'expected N, got M' on a cross-package call, confirm the callee's real signature first: this analyzer skips the check precisely because it cannot see the signature, so a report here means it did see one.,} FOpMismatch => Advice::{ why : One of four shapes: `!` applied to a non-boolean; a binary operator applied to operand types it does not accept; a value that is known not to be callable being called; or a list index that is not an integer. A callee whose type is `Unknown` is never reported — an unresolved type is not evidence of anything., how : For an operand error, check both sides against the operator's domain. For 'not callable', the callee's type is known and is not a function — name a function, or call the method on the receiver. For a list index, pass an Int.,} FMethodError => Advice::{ why : The behavioral lens could not find a method matching the operator or function on the abstract values it computed for the operands. It reasons about the concrete values it can fold, so it is the lens that reports most precisely and the one least likely to be the tool's blindness., how : Confirm the receiver type and the method's parameter types at the call site. This family is raised by the behavioral lens on folded constant values, so a finding usually corresponds to a real compile error.,} FCondBool => Advice::{ why : A condition's type is known and is not boolean. As with the operand checks, an `Unknown` condition is never reported., how : Make the condition a boolean expression — compare explicitly, or replace a non-boolean value with a test on it.,} FUndefinedName => Advice::{ why : No visible binding for the name: not declared in this file, not a builtin, and not present in the cross-file symbol table. The wording says which lens saw it — `no visible binding` (structural), `undefined name` (type), `undefined variable` / `undefined function` (behavior). All three consult the same table, so one finding means all three looked., how : Declare it, import it, or — when it lives in another package — index that package's interface with `--extern-iface-dir <dir>` (target `.repos/` after `moon fetch`). TWO known limits, both unfixable from the CLI: a `#doc(hidden)` API appears in no `.mbti` and so cannot be indexed that way, and a top-level cross-package reference written `@pkg.fn(1, 2)` is not folded into a callable name by the parser, so it is reported even when the package is indexed.,} FUnreachable => Advice::{ why : UNREACHABLE CODE: no execution reaches this statement, because the flow arriving at it has already left the block. The behavioral lens decides this while executing the body, and it joins branches -- so a `return` inside an `if` does NOT by itself make what follows dead, and code after an `if` whose EVERY branch terminates does. CAVEAT, measured: when a callee's parameter was bound from the CALLER's argument, a branch decided by that value can kill the rest of the body on one input, and the finding is then WRONG -- `fn f(c : Bool) -> Int { if c { return 1 } return 2 }` called as f(true) reports `return 2`, which f(false) runs. Treat a finding inside a function called with a literal argument as unverified. The three deck situations are separate: this family is unreachable code, DEAD CODE (a value overwritten before use) is reported by NO family, and an INFEASIBLE PATH is MSA-013 and says `D[P]`., how : Delete the statement. If it was meant to run, the control flow above it needs to change. When the finding is in a function that receives a literal argument from a call site, first check whether the function is also called with other values: if it is, the statement runs for those and the finding is the over-report described above, not a defect.,} FStaleNosec => Advice::{ why : A `// nosec` comment on this line suppressed NOTHING. The comment names a finding family, and no finding of that family was reported here -- so the defect it used to silence is gone, or was never there, or the family id in the comment does not exist. A suppression that suppresses nothing is dead weight in the source, and it is a sign that the code it referred to has changed., how : Delete the comment. If the comment is still needed, the finding it was meant to silence is not being reported -- check the family id against the roster (`MSA-001` and up) and check that the line is the line the finding is on.,} FInfeasibleBranch => Advice::{ why : The guards on the way to this branch contradict this one, so the conjunction on its path is unsatisfiable and its domain is EMPTY: no value of the bindings involved reaches it. This is the constraint-level counterpart of `Unreachable` -- the flow arriving here is well formed, and it is the VALUES that cannot arrive. The finding quotes the path condition it negated, so the claim can be checked by hand., how : Either the more recent guard is wrong (it can never hold, so the branch is dead and should be deleted), or an earlier one is (its bound is too tight for the later test to be reachable). Find the two guards named in the finding and decide which one was meant. Only comparisons of an IMMUTABLE binding against a literal contribute facts, so a contradictory guard over a mutated or computed value is NOT reported here -- it is counted undecided.,} FRedundantGuard => Advice::{ why : The guards before this test already force its outcome, so it cannot take the other way and decides nothing. Unlike a constant condition, nothing here is literally constant: the test is redundant only in the context of the path that reaches it., how : Remove the test, or, if the earlier guard's bound looks wrong, fix that one -- a redundant test is frequently the symptom of a bound that was meant to be tighter. Kept as a finding rather than a notice because a test that cannot fail removes the safety the reader believes it provides.,} FDeadStore => Advice::{ why : The value this write put in the name is read on no path: every way out of here either writes the name again before reading it or leaves the function. The binding itself may be used elsewhere -- this is about ONE write, which is why the finding is a liveness result and not an unused-local one. A DECLARATION is one write too, and it is reported here only when the name IS read somewhere, so this family and `UnusedLocal` cannot report one line for one fact., how : Delete the write, or move it to where its value is actually wanted. If the right-hand side has effects you need, keep those and drop only the binding. For a declaration the fix is the same: the initialiser is overwritten before anything reads it, so the initialiser can go -- but keep the binding itself if the name is read later. Reported as a finding because a value nobody reads is dead weight the reader is paying for at runtime and, more importantly, it usually means the value they expected to be there came from somewhere else.,} FDivisionByZero => Advice::{ why : The divisor of this division is zero on EVERY path that reaches it, so the division raises a division-by-zero when the program runs. The claim comes from a sign analysis: the divisor's sign was pinned to zero by the transfer functions, and the analysis reports only what it can pin down -- an unknown sign is never reported, so this is a must-finding and not a maybe. The toolchain does not catch this shape: `moon check` exits 0 on `1 / 0`., how : Give the divisor a value that is not zero -- check the value that reaches it, and check the guard that was supposed to prevent it. If the division is deliberate, test the divisor first and return or raise on the zero case, which also makes the intent explicit.,} FNegativeIndex => Advice::{ why : The index of this subscript is negative on EVERY path that reaches it, so the subscript is out of bounds when the program runs. The claim comes from a sign analysis: the index's sign was pinned to negative, and an unknown sign is never reported, so this is a must-finding and not a maybe. The toolchain does not catch this shape either: `moon check` exits 0 on `arr[-1]`., how : Fix the index -- the usual cause is an index computed as `i - 1` or `i - offset` that goes below zero, or an offset that is larger than the base. If a negative index is meant to mean 'from the end', the language spells that differently and this finding is the analyzer telling you the two were confused.,} FTaintFlow => Advice::{ why : Data from a source you named may reach a sensitive argument of this sink. The claim comes from the security deck's own analysis: a tainted datum is an OBJECT, it is carried by the pointer analysis, and a flow is a triple of (source call site, sink call site, argument index). The claim is a MAY claim -- the analysis reports a flow it cannot rule out -- and it is only as good as your specification: the analysis knows what you called a source and what you called a sink, and it knows nothing about which of them are actually sensitive. The toolchain does not catch this shape: `moon check` says nothing about where a value came from., how : Decide what this sink's sensitive argument must not receive, and remove the taint before the data reaches it -- pass a length, a boolean, a redacted string, or a value that has been through a scrubbing step. If the flow is intended, then the specification is what needs fixing rather than the code: the source and the sink you named are the ones the analyzer takes as untrusted and sensitive, and a finding nobody can act on is a finding everybody learns to ignore.,}}
